findings.body: **`CHANGELOG.md:8`** — no `## Unreleased` section exists (top section is `## v0.6.0`), so this PR adds no changelog entry. `.maintainer.yaml` sets `release.autoRelease: true`, and the release agent promotes `## Unreleased` → `## vX.Y.Z` after merge — with no section, merging lands the CVE fix on master but never ships a release to consumers. Repo precedent: the prior lockfile-only security bump (`c6f136a`) did add a `### Fixed` entry. Fix — insert directly above line 8: *(rule: `changelog/unreleased-entry-required`)* ```markdown ## Unreleased ### Fixed - fix: Bump `fast-uri` from 3.1.4 to 3.1.5 in `mcp/` (transitive via `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` → `ajv`), patching CVE-2026-18446 / GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7 (high, CVSS 7.5) — host confusion via backslash authority introducer. ```

review_command: claude --print --model opus --effort xhigh --permission-mode bypassPermissions '/coding:pr-review bench-base-20 full'

findings.body: **`pkg/factory/runner.go:104-106`** — a live, write-scoped GitHub App installation token is injected into the Claude subprocess env unconditionally, including under `--skip-post`; nothing in this PR ties `GH_TOKEN` injection to `cfg.SkipPost`. The flag nils out the Go-side poster/verifier only. The documented guarantee — "suppresses **all** GitHub write calls" (`CHANGELOG.md:11`, `README.md:29`, `CLAUDE.md:87`, and the flag's own usage string at `cmd/run-task/main.go:76`) — is therefore false at the credential level. The only things preventing a write are the fixed per-phase tool allowlists (`pkg/factory/factory.go:40-85`, untouched by this PR, no `gh pr review`/`gh api`/`curl`) and prompt prose ("Do NOT post anything to the PR", `pkg/prompts/review_workflow.md:28`) which is advisory to the LLM, not enforced. The flag's stated purpose is pointing the reviewer at *third-party* PRs — i.e. exactly the untrusted-content/prompt-injection threat model where that distinction matters, and no `SkipPost`-specific test pins the allowlist invariant, so it can regress silently. Fix by either minting/injecting no token (or a read-scoped one) when `SkipPost` is true, or by rewording all four claim sites to state the real mechanism.

**`pkg/steps_checkout_execution.go:316`** — the nil-poster early return fires before `ParseVerdict` (:328), before the fail-closed `!funnelRan && approve → request-changes` gate (:338-340), and before `appendDiagnosticsSection` (:376). A `--skip-post` run therefore never computes the effective gated verdict and writes no diagnostics, which weakens the "findings are still written to the task file" claim — the operator gets review prose but not the verdict the same review would have posted.

**`pkg/factory/runner_test.go:32-33`** — `Expect(poster).To(BeNil())` cannot detect the regression this PR is themed around. Gomega's `BeNil()` falls through to `reflect.ValueOf(x).IsNil()` for pointer/interface kinds, so it passes for a typed-nil concrete pointer boxed in the `PrPoster` interface — precisely the value for which the production guards (`s.prPoster == nil`, `s.poster == nil`) would *not* fire. The assertion reads as proof of the nil-interface contract but structurally cannot provide it.

**`pkg/skip_post_boundary_test.go:169-226`** — case 4's stated failure mechanism is wrong. The comment claims absence of an `ai_review verify:` line in `## Diagnostics` is the negative signal, but `appendVerifyDiagnostic` (`pkg/steps_review.go:253`) only runs when verification **fails**; and on the typed-nil regression it guards against, `VerifyReview` would panic on its first receiver deref (`pkg/githubposter/verifier.go:68`) long before any diagnostic could be built. Ginkgo still fails the spec via panic capture, but the documented discriminator is dead — a successful live GitHub read would leave no diagnostic and pass silently.

**`pkg/skip_post_boundary_test.go:102-166`** — case 3 does not exercise the skip-post contract it is labelled with. `ResolvePosters(RunConfig{SkipPost:true})` can only ever return `(nil, nil)`, so the "nil poster + non-nil verifier" combination is manufactured by discarding the real verifier and substituting `mocks.ReviewVerifier`; and with `verdict="pass"`, `tryDismissHallucinated` — the sole reader of `s.poster` — is never reached. It duplicates the existing "verification runs and succeeds" case at `pkg/steps_review_test.go:298-317`.

**`cmd/run-task/main.go:171`** — the `SkipPost: a.SkipPost` pass-through and its counterpart call site at `pkg/factory/runner.go:136` are the only untested lines of the change: `cmd/run-task/main_test.go` asserts nothing beyond "Compiles", and `RunAgent` has no test. Meanwhile `ResolvePosters` itself carries four tests. A refactor that dropped the `ResolvePosters` call from `RunAgent` — restoring the unconditional `Create*` calls — would leave every test in this PR green.

**`pkg/factory/factory.go:166-173`** — `CreateAgent`'s doc comment states the execution phase "posts review to GitHub via PrPoster" unconditionally, and parenthesises only the verifier case ("nil verifier skips verification"). With a nil poster now a supported wiring, the execution line is flatly wrong and the asymmetry is misleading.

**`CHANGELOG.md:11`** — one `feat:` bullet bundles three concerns: the new flag (`feat:`), the nil-poster panic guard in `tryDismissHallucinated` (`fix:`), and the CLI doc re-attribution (`docs:`). Split into three bullets so bump classification and changelog scanning stay accurate. *(rule: `changelog/conventional-prefix-required`)*

**`docs/pr-post-back.md:128`** — "This preserves backward compatibility with the local CLI mode" is now false. Before this PR `cmd/run-task` never produced a nil poster (that was the documented-vs-actual mismatch this PR fixes); nil-poster is new opt-in behaviour behind a flag defaulting to `false`, and the default path is unchanged. Commit `5ab6ccd` fixed the sentence before it but left this one.

**`pkg/factory/runner.go:51-53`** — `RunConfig.Agent`'s comment still frames the nil-`Agent` branch as "cmd/run-task leaves this nil so CreateAgent is used for backward compatibility". That branch is now the load-bearing mechanism through which `SkipPost` takes effect; the backward-compat framing understates it.

**`docs/pr-post-back.md:126`** — heading `## nil Poster — Local / Backward-Compatible Mode` carries the same stale framing as the line-128 finding; update both together (e.g. "Local Opt-In (`--skip-post`) Mode").

**`pkg/skip_post_boundary_test.go:64-100`** — case 2 and `pkg/steps_review_test.go:614-627` case (j) drive an identical scenario (verdict=fail + hallucinations + nil poster) and assert the same two outcomes; the only difference is `ResolvePosters`-sourced nil vs literal `nil`, which are behaviourally identical today. Keep one.

**`pkg/factory/runner.go:66`** — `ResolvePosters` is exported solely so `pkg/skip_post_boundary_test.go` (a different package's test binary, where an `export_test.go` alias would be invisible) can reach it. Legitimate Go constraint and consistent with the `ResolveBotLogin` precedent, but worth a one-line comment saying so.

findings.body: **`task/recurring-schedules/prod/plan-weekend.yaml:65`** — `{{next_sun_date}}` is the first use of a non-`{{current_date}}` placeholder in a `frontmatter:` field anywhere in this repo. On the base branch all 74 frontmatter placeholder occurrences are `{{current_date}}`; `{{next_sun_date}}` appeared exactly once, in *body prose* (this same file, line 18). Body and frontmatter are rendered by `recurring-task-creator` (image `v0.10.2`), whose source is not in this config-only repo, and no placeholder set is documented here. If the frontmatter renderer supports a narrower set than the body renderer, 7 prod tasks get the literal string `{{next_sun_date}}` in a date field. Same exposure at `check-ftmo-demo-accounts.yaml:65`, `lexoffice-invoices.yaml`, `moneymoney-review.yaml`, `plan-next-week.yaml:67`, `renew-gmail-oauth-tokens.yaml:64`, `weekly-review.yaml`. **This is an unverified risk, not a proven defect** — I have no cluster access from here. Gate the prod apply on a dev-stage render: trigger `https://dev.quant.benjamin-borbe.de/admin/recurring-task-creator/trigger` and confirm the generated task's `due_date` is a real date.

**`task/recurring-schedules/prod/renew-gmail-oauth-tokens.yaml:64`** — `due_date: "{{next_sun_date}}"` on a task whose own body (line 18) states "Google's tokens expire every 7 days for unverified apps". The schedule is weekly-Saturday, so the token's hard expiry lands on the Saturday the task fires. A Sunday due date sanctions consuming the entire safety margin and then some — a token that lapses means trading-relevant email is silently un-ingested (the body's stated failure mode). Should be `{{current_date}}` like the other hard-deadline Saturday items. Contrast `check-ftmo-demo-accounts.yaml`, where a Sunday due date is fine because that task builds in its own 7-day lookahead ("flag anything ≤ 7 days", line 41).

**`task/recurring-schedules/prod/plan-weekend.yaml:65`** — `due_date: "{{next_sun_date}}"` contradicts the task it annotates. Body line 18: "as the first thing Saturday morning"; the plan covers Sat→Sun; `priority: 1`. A Sunday due date means the task is not overdue until the window it exists to plan has already closed. Should be `{{current_date}}`.

**`task/recurring-schedules/dev/docker-registry-gc.yaml:67`** — left without `due_date` while its prod sibling `prod/docker-registry-gc.yaml` got one. It is `recurrence: Weekday, weekday: Saturday` — squarely in the class this PR targets. Creates dev/prod drift in the only component that has both stages. Add `due_date: "{{current_date}}"` after line 67.

**`task/recurring-schedules/prod/plan-next-week.yaml:27-29`** — Success Criteria was rewritten to cover priorities, acceptance criteria, and `# Explicitly Deferred`, but Tasks line 43 also requires allocating to `# Order of Work`, which neither Success Criteria nor the DoD (line 49) checks. Add it to one of them, or drop it from line 43.

**`task/recurring-schedules/prod/plan-next-week.yaml:29`** — "Month link present (target may not exist yet if the monthly plan is deferred)" explicitly sanctions a dead wikilink. Defensible for a note that will exist later, but it sits against commit `6db0dc9` ("fix dead `[[Tech]]` theme link in recurring task templates") from two commits back. Worth a one-line rationale in the criterion so the next dead-link sweep doesn't "fix" it.

findings.body: **`src/server.ts:31`** — `export type CreateApp` is hand-written and never bound to `createApp` (line 40), so `tsc` never compares the declared contract to the implementation; the only bridge is `require()`, which is `any`. I verified this in an isolated probe: an alias deliberately declaring `(name: string) => number` against an implementation returning an object produced `TSC_EXIT=0`. The node agent reproduced it independently in-repo by adding a mandatory second parameter to the real `createApp` — `tsc --noEmit` still exited 0, including at the call sites now passing too few arguments. This PR adds to `CLAUDE.md` that `typecheck` is "the only gate that makes the types mean anything"; for every cross-module boundary that claim is currently false, and the skeleton propagates it to every service cloned from here. Fix: `const createApp: CreateApp = ({ isReady }: CreateAppOptions = {}) => {…}` — I confirmed that `export type CreateApp = typeof createApp` makes the same drift fail with `TS2322`/`TS2559`.

**`src/handlers/health.ts:12`** — same defect: `HealthRouter` is asserted, not derived, and `healthRouter` (line 27) carries no annotation tying it to the alias. Note `src/config.ts:34` and `src/log.ts:42` are *not* affected — their object literals carry the annotation, so those two interfaces are genuinely checked. The fix is to make the two factories match that existing in-repo pattern.

**`package.json:8`** — `"node": ">=22"` no longer matches what the code requires. Node ships unflagged type-stripping only from **22.18.0**; on 22.6–22.17 it needs `--experimental-strip-types`, and below 22.6 it does not exist. A contributor on Node 22.14 passes `npm ci` (engines satisfied) and then gets an opaque parse/extension failure from `make run`, `make test`, and `npm start`. Bump to `">=22.18.0"`.

**`src/server.ts:69`** — the error handler types `err: Error`, narrower than the shipped `ErrorRequestHandler`, which I confirmed declares `err: any` (`@types/express-serve-static-core/index.d.ts:77`). Express 5 auto-forwards rejected-promise values to `next()`, and a rejection reason need not be an `Error`. On `throw 'boom'` or `Promise.reject({code:500})`, `err.message`/`err.stack` log as `undefined` with no type error. Use `err: unknown` plus `err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)`.

**`test/health.test.ts`** — `config.check()` is the PR's new startup-validation logic and has zero coverage; `test/` contains only `health.test.ts`, which never imports config. Neither the invalid-`PORT` nor the invalid-`SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS` branch is exercised. Worth naming in the fix: because `config` reads `process.env` at import time, a test needs a fresh module registry (`delete require.cache[...]`) or a child process — which is itself a signal the singleton-plus-`check()` shape is awkward to verify.

**`eslint.config.js:44`** — the comment ("enum, namespace, and parameter-property syntax would make `node src/*.ts` require a build step") sits directly above `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` and `no-non-null-assertion`, neither of which has anything to do with erasable syntax. That guard is `erasableSyntaxOnly` in `tsconfig.json` (plus inherited `no-namespace`). `CLAUDE.md` says every non-obvious invariant gets a comment saying *why* — this one points at the wrong mechanism, and a future service inherits the misdirection.

**`eslint.config.js:16`** — `tseslint.config(...)` is marked `@deprecated` in the pinned typescript-eslint 8.66.0; I confirmed the annotation at `typescript-eslint/dist/config-helper.d.ts:67` ("ESLint core now provides this functionality via `defineConfig()`, which we now recommend instead"). Nothing breaks today, but a skeleton shouldn't seed every future service with a deprecated entry point. `eslint@9.39.5` exports `./config`, so the change is `const { defineConfig } = require('eslint/config')` and the block shape stays identical.

**`test/health.test.ts:22`** — `? address.port : 0` silently falls back to port 0 instead of failing. If the invariant ever breaks, every test in the file fetches `http://127.0.0.1:0` and reports a connection error rather than the real cause. Throw, mirroring the `isRecord` guard the same file already uses at line 10.

**`eslint.config.js:39-55`** — `CLAUDE.md` bans "`any`, `as`, `!`, `@ts-ignore`". Three are enforced (`no-explicit-any`, `no-non-null-assertion`, inherited `ban-ts-comment`); `as` is enforced by nothing, and it's fully erasable so `erasableSyntaxOnly` won't catch it. No `as` appears in this diff — but the invariant is currently aspirational. Add `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-assertions` if it's meant to hold.
**`README.md:107`** — the new License section links the file without naming the license; the repo's own README template names it inline (`BSD-2-Clause — see [LICENSE](./LICENSE).`).

findings.body: **`.github/workflows/ci.yml:32`** — `wget -qO - … | sudo apt-key add -` installs Aqua's signing key into apt's **global** trusted keyring, where it can authenticate packages from *any* configured repo, including the Ubuntu archives. That is a trust-scope widening shipped inside a PR whose stated purpose is hardening. Separately, `apt-key` is deprecated since Ubuntu 20.10 and non-functional on 24.04 (`ubuntu-latest`) per most sources — reports conflict on whether the binary is absent or merely warns, but a hard failure here means the gate this PR adds never runs in CI. Fix: replace the whole block with `- uses: aquasecurity/setup-trivy@v0.3.1` (official, supports `version:` pinning), or dearmor to `/etc/apt/keyrings/trivy.gpg` and add `[signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/trivy.gpg]` to the sources line.

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml:35`** — `apt-get install -y trivy` is unpinned, so every CI run takes whatever is latest. Trivy minor releases add detectors and change exit semantics, so CI can go red with no code change, and an upstream compromise lands unreviewed. Note the inconsistency: this PR pins `PIP_AUDIT_VERSION ?= 2.9.0` two files over. `setup-trivy` takes a `version:` input.

**`README.md:80`** and **`Makefile.precommit:36`** — "covers the exact transitive tree that gets installed" is not accurate. `make audit` runs `uv export --all-extras` (includes the `dev` extra: pytest, pytest-asyncio, httpx, ruff, mypy — `pyproject.toml:26-32`), while `Dockerfile:16` runs `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-editable` with no extras. The audited set is a strict superset of what ships. Reword to "the full resolved dependency set including dev tooling — broader than the production image".

**`Makefile.precommit:42`** — the comment promises that unreachable findings "get an explicit `--ignore-vuln` entry with a reason", but no such surface exists: no file, no make variable, nothing in the recipe. Combined with auditing dev dependencies at **zero severity threshold**, a single dev-only advisory in ruff/mypy/pytest hard-blocks `make precommit` and all CI repo-wide until someone hand-edits the recipe. This is exactly the gap `.trivyignore` was created to close for the other scanner — add a `PIP_AUDIT_IGNORE ?=` variable or an equivalent reason-annotated file.

**`pyproject.toml:64-68`** — `ignore = ["S104"]` disables hardcoded-bind-all-interfaces across the entire repo. There are 4 hits: `src/skeleton/server.py:9`, `src/skeleton/__main__.py:33`, and 2 in `tests/test_server.py`. The two src bindings are intentional, but the global ignore also means a *future* bind-all — a debug or admin port — will never be flagged. Prefer `# noqa: S104` with the reason at the two src sites and add `S104` to the `tests/**` per-file-ignores, keeping the rule live everywhere else. This is the same "keep it honest" standard the PR sets for `.trivyignore` in the file it just created.

**`Makefile.precommit:24`** — `check: lint typecheck audit trivy` makes the default target and `make precommit` hard-require a local `trivy` binary plus network egress (trivy DB from ghcr, pip-audit advisories from PyPI). Previously `check` was fully local. A fresh clone without trivy gets an opaque `make: trivy: Command not found`, and README documents `make trivy` usage but not installation. Add install instructions, and consider keeping `precommit` local while a separate target carries the network gates.

**`README.md:76-94`** — the whole "Security gates" section is design rationale, not user-facing content: why a make target depends on `sync` (line 82), why `osv-scanner` was rejected (line 86), and a three-repo gate comparison table (lines 90-94). Move to `docs/security.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, leaving 1-2 sentences in README. *(rule: `readme/user-facing-not-agent-context`)*

**`CHANGELOG.md:18`** — `- ci: install trivy in CI` uses a prefix outside the recognised set. The guide's table defines exactly seven (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `test:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `perf:`), with `chore:` covering "Dependency updates, build, tooling". Use `chore:`. *(rule: `changelog/conventional-prefix-required`)*
**`.github/workflows/ci.yml:33`** — `sudo tee -a` appends, so a re-run duplicates the repo line. Use `tee` without `-a`.
**`.github/workflows/ci.yml:38`** — `uv sync --all-extras` is redundant; `make precommit` runs `sync` as its first prerequisite.

**`Makefile.precommit:60-61`** — the `$(ROOTDIR)/.trivyignore` fallback is unreachable today: the scan target is always literal `.`, so when make runs from the repo root the first `$(wildcard .trivyignore)` branch always wins.
**`README.md:84`** — the S104/S101 suppression rationale duplicates the comments already in `pyproject.toml:65-67` and `pyproject.toml:71`, which will drift.
